newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mar housing completions fell 10.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mar housing completions fell 10.4 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department report on completions of new privately-owned housing units, seasonally adjusted annual rates, in 1,000s, with percent changes from
prior months and year over year.
Housing completions by region, seasonally adj., in 1,000s:

Commerce said March completions of single-family homes fell 12.0 percent after a revised 13.4 percent rise in February and a revised 5.8 percent decrease in January. Previously, the department said single-family completions rose 9.3 percent in February and decreased 6.0 percent in January.

March multi-family unit completions fell 3.9 percent after a revised 20.6 percent rise in February and a revised 17.6 percent decrease in January. Previously, the department said February multi-family unit completions rose 17.5 percent and that January multi-family unit completions fell 17.9 percent.

The department said actual completions on an unadjusted basis fell in March to 103,900 units from 104,100 units in February but rose from 95,700 units in January. In March 1996, actual completions were reported at 103,100.

Privately-owned housing units under construction fell to a seasonally adjusted 819,000 in March from 825,000 in February but were up from 818,000 in January. They compare with 814,000 units under construction in March 1996.
